The Free Dinner Pitch

lines.text: That free steak dinner could be the priciest meal you ever eat.
lines.say: That free steak dinner could be the priciest meal you ever eat.

lines.text: In a 2007 report, US regulators examined 110 free-lunch investment seminars.
lines.say: In a two thousand seven report, US regulators examined one hundred ten free lunch investment seminars.

lines.text: 100% were sales pitches dressed up as classes.
lines.say: One hundred percent were sales pitches dressed up as classes.
Fifty percent used exaggerated or misleading advertising.
And twenty-three percent involved possibly unsuitable investments.

lines.text: Scams keep growing. FTC reports show investment-scam losses went from $3.8 billion in 2022 to $7.9 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Scams keep growing. F T C reports show investment scam losses went from three point eight billion dollars in twenty twenty-two to seven point nine billion in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Our math: that's about double in three years.
lines.say: By our math, that's about double in just three years.

lines.text: Red flags: guaranteed returns, sign-today pressure, fancy "senior" titles. Check sellers on BrokerCheck, the SEC site, or your state regulator.
lines.say: Red flags are guaranteed returns, pressure to sign today, and fancy senior titles. Check sellers on BrokerCheck, the S E C site, or with your state regulator.

post.title: Free investment dinners: what regulators found in 110 checks
post.ig:
That free steak dinner could be the priciest meal you ever eat.
In a 2007 joint review of 110 free-lunch investment seminars, regulators found every one was a sales pitch.
50% used exaggerated or misleading ads; 23% involved possibly unsuitable investments.
FTC data: reported investment-scam losses hit $7.9 billion in 2025, up from $3.8 billion in 2022.
Check any seller on FINRA BrokerCheck, the SEC adviser site, or with your state regulator.
Sources: SEC/NASAA/FINRA 2007 report; FTC Consumer Sentinel.
News and education, not financial advice.
